source.title: Information-Theoretic Local Minima Characterization and Regularization

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether measured local-minimum properties track generalization and whether a regularizer derived from the proposed metric changes test error. Uses different measures and interventions from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own CIFAR-10 experiments varying confusion-set size, data augmentation, and batch size, the measured metric comparisons, and the regularizer’s reported test errors. Cited findings about other methods are not extracted as rows. The paper does not test random-label memorization versus natural-label generalization in the sense of V1.
record.test_reason: The study tests V5 by varying batch size and measuring held-out classification error under a fixed 200-epoch budget. Its Fisher determinant and Hessian measures do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their Fisher-information-based metric characterizes generalization differences among local minima and that its derived regularizer improves generalization across the tested networks. These conclusions concern their metric, not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures a Fisher-information determinant approximation and introduces a gradient-based regularizer derived from it; it does not reproduce the magnitude-aware perturbation measure or interventions in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The metric’s comparative performance varies by scenario: it works across confusion-set sizes and data augmentation schemes; in the batch-size scenario the text says all metrics except robustness capture the trend. Regularization is applied in the middle and late training stages; the paper says applying it at the beginning can cause numerical errors.

fits_no_version.finding: Across confusion-set sizes, the Fisher determinant approximation and both Hessian measures track test error; across augmentation schemes only the proposed metric succeeds; across batch sizes all except robustness capture the trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A sampled Fisher log-determinant can indicate test-error differences among ResNet-20 minima with similarly low training losses, with comparative performance depending on how the minima are generated.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed regularizer reduces mean held-out error in all reported CIFAR comparisons and both ImageNet validation measures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A Fisher-derived regularizer applied after the first learning-rate drop can improve image-classification performance across the tested convolutional architectures.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119, 2020
record.problems: The batch-size scenario's exact test-error values are only in figures in the supplied text; the reported metric relationships are described qualitatively. The experiments use ResNet-20 for metric comparisons. The regularizer's coefficient is selected by validation; experiments report means and standard deviations over five CIFAR runs and three ImageNet runs.
record.rows_left_out: No row-valued comparisons were extracted from cited prior work. Figure 2–4 exact plotted metric and test-error values are not recoverable from the supplied text; relevant qualitative outcomes are captured in R5–R7, and per-batch test error rows R1–R4 retain figure-only values.

untested.parts: No natural-label versus fully random-label comparison establishing near-perfect fitting and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy. The mixed confusion-set experiment does not supply this comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or test of learned local connectivity.
No optimizer comparison; claims about adaptive methods are citations to prior studies.

No language models, longer-training comparison, learning-rate scaling with warmup, normalization intervention, or systematic identification of the batch-size threshold. Only ResNet-20/CIFAR-10 with batches 128–1024 is tested.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of its gap rankings against norm- and margin-based measures. Fisher determinant and unscaled Hessian metrics measure different quantities.
No influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V5. The batch-size verdict rests on the explicit qualitative result in Figure 4, without reconstructing plotted values or inferring statistical significance. For rows linked to no version, cannot_determine concerns the listed claims, not the readability of the reported regularizer results.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of fitting random labels against generalization on natural labels.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Only batch sizes 128, 256, 512, and 1024 on ResNet-20/CIFAR-10; no language models, workload-dependent threshold analysis, or adaptive recipe comparisons.

Tests the proposed Fisher-information determinant approximation and compares it with robustness, Hessian Frobenius norm, and spectral radius, but does not test magnitude-aware sharpness as specified in the version.

relationships.condition: ResNet-20 on CIFAR-10, batches 128, 256, 512 and 1024, fixed 200 epochs, initial learning rate 0.1 reduced on training-loss plateaus
relationships.reason: Section 7.1 and Figure 4 explicitly report worse generalization with larger batches despite similarly small final training losses and essentially perfect training accuracy; R1–R4 record this sweep, although individual errors are unavailable.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest worse generalization with larger batches despite similarly low training losses and nearly perfect training accuracy. Individual test-error values were not provided.
